text:
Ana Muñoz: kicking off SEA2 burst cluster bring-up. I pushed the initial terraform, need a quick smoke pass + network validation before we hand to SRE for canary traffic.
Kevin Park: ack. I can run the infra smoke tests now — ping me when the bootstrap EC2s are up.
DevOps Bot: deploy started by @ana at 1799999999. Plan OK. Applying 6 resources.
Ana Muñoz: bootstrap done, nodes in ASG are in Pending -> InService. GPUs: 8x A400 per node across 3 nodes (24 GPUs).
Maria Chen: noted. I'll validate kube node readiness and NVidia drivers. Running `kubectl get nodes -o wide` now.
Kevin Park: quick checklist I want covered in this thread: 1) kernel + driver check, 2) CVMFS mount if needed, 3) network egress to model registry + S3, 4) latency to primary region ~<25ms, 5) billing tag propagation.
Samir Patel: I'll do perf smoke: load 3 concurrent small generations to warm KV cache + measure p50/p95.
Maria Chen: driver: `nvidia-smi` shows CUDA 12.1, driver 535.92, all GPUs visible. kube node labels: `gpu=true, region=sea2`.
Maria Chen: found one node with kubelet crashlooping on cgroup v2. Quick fix: bumped kubelet flag --cgroups-per-qos=false and restarted systemd. Node rejoined.
Kevin Park: good catch. Add to runbook note: "ensure kubelet flags compatible with AMI cgroup mode".
Samir Patel: perf smoke: starting 3x short runs with our tst-model (seq len 64). p50=22ms, p95=78ms, tail occasionally 320ms during cold KV loads.
Ana Muñoz: those numbers look within SLOs (p95 < 100ms). document cold tail behavior in readiness review.
Kevin Park: network tests: `curl -sS --resolve registry.redwood.internal:443:10.2.5.12 https://registry.redwood.internal/health` -> 200 OK. Egress to S3 (us-east-1) RTT 75ms — acceptable for warm cache but may affect first-token pulls.
DevOps Bot: smoke-test-suite finished with 1 warning (kubelet cgroup flag fixed). All other checks green.
Maria Chen: NVLink status: PCI topology OK, driver reports no ECC errors. Disk: root 30% used, model cache disk 22%.
Samir Patel: cost check: estimated incremental hourly cost ~ $16/hr for 3-node pool at current spot prices, on-demand fallback still configured. I kicked off a reserved-capacity request for finance to review for steady state.
Kevin Park: gating items before handoff -> 1) 0 critical alerts, 2) p95 latency < 100ms for smoke workload, 3) kube node readiness 100%, 4) network egress to model registry 200 OK, 5) billing tags present. Current status: all satisfied except billing tags — missing `cost-center` on ASG.
Ana Muñoz: added billing tag via terraform patch, re-applied. Please verify tag propagation.
DevOps Bot: terraform apply complete at 1800000020. Tags: env=staging, cost-center=research.
Kevin Park: confirmed cost-center tag present in ASG and instances.
Maria Chen: running one last canary: route 2% traffic from canary-svc to sea2 nodes using traffic controller. Command: `trafficctl set-weight canary-svc sea2 2`
Samir Patel: canary warmups look stable, token cost per request unchanged, perf stable over 5 minutes.
oncall-bot: incident watch enabled for SEA2 for next 60 minutes. Alert policy: gpu_temp_high, node_reboot, deploy_failure.
Ana Muñoz: ready for handoff to SRE for 4-hour monitored canary and final readiness review. I've added the short summary to the runbook: "SEA2 burst cluster: 3 nodes, 24 GPUs, driver 535.92, p95 smoke 78ms, one kubelet cgroup flag patched, billing tags applied."
Kevin Park: +1 from infra. SRE — please confirm takeover in this thread and start your checklist.
Samir Patel: leaving a note in the runbook about cold KV tail: recommend enabling prefix caching for common prompt sets (helps first-token tail).
SRE (placeholder): (waiting on SRE ack)
Ana Muñoz: pinging #eng-sre for takeover. @oncall-sre please review when available.
